_status_note: DRAFT gold case file for PMC11890614 (Case Library task L1.3, curation steps 1-5). The Case Reviewer (Dr Atul Tiwari) must verify every fact against the article before it is frozen as PMC11890614@v1. Values are transcribed as printed in the article (US conventional units: g/dL, 10^3/uL, ng/mL); unit conversion waits for the pilot review. Day 0 is admission (the article's hospital day 1), so the article's hospital day N is day N-1 here. Many work-up results are undated in the text (their dates are probably in Figure 5, an image not read here): they carry day null and a note. Items under 'gaps' are NOT article facts. Path analysis and affected values wait for the pilot review.

vignette: A 36-year-old man, originally from Haiti and with no significant past medical history, presents to the emergency department with four months of recurrent fever and a dry cough.
opening_statement_lay: I've had fevers on and off and a dry cough for about four months now, and they just won't go away.

facts.release_text: Originally from Haiti; he immigrated from there.
Night sweats over the same four months.
Unintentional weight loss over the same four months. Amount not recorded.
Started on high-dose steroid after the work-up for infection was negative. Drug and dose not recorded.

final_dx.text: Miliary tuberculosis with repeatedly negative initial microbiological tests, mistaken for sarcoidosis on non-necrotising granulomas, treated with high-dose steroid and complicated by secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
secondary_findings: Secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (fever, cytopenias, ferritin 7821 ng/mL, raised soluble IL-2 receptor and CXCL9, haemophagocytes in the marrow; H-score 256)

accepted_differential: Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis from another trigger (EBV, lymphoma)
red_herrings: Negative sputum AFB smears, MTB PCR and mycobacterial cultures
Negative first cell-free DNA and MicroGenDX sequencing
Non-necrotising (non-caseating) granulomas in the lung and marrow
key_discriminators: Miliary pattern on chest imaging with four months of fever, cough, night sweats and weight loss
The low sensitivity of every single TB test in miliary disease
No response to high-dose steroid, then worsening
Pancytopenia with rising ferritin and transaminases (secondary haemophagocytosis)
Repeat NGS, second lavage AFB stain and PCR positive on day 25
ground_truth.treatment_given: High-dose steroid for presumed sarcoidosis; then high-dose steroids and etoposide (HLH-2004); empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics and antifungals, intubation and vasopressors from day 18; rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol from day 25 with HLH chemotherapy withheld.
ground_truth.outcome: Multi-organ failure; died about one week after starting anti-tuberculosis treatment. Autopsy declined, so whether tuberculosis was present from the start or reactivated under immunosuppression is not proven; the authors think it was present from the start.
must_do: Keep tuberculosis high on the list despite negative tests, given the miliary pattern, the symptoms and the origin
Start empirical anti-tuberculosis treatment when suspicion stays high despite negative tests, or cover with it before any steroid
Send tissue from more than one site (lung, marrow, liver) for AFB stain, MTB PCR and mycobacterial culture, and repeat testing when the course changes
Recognise secondary haemophagocytosis (cytopenias, ferritin, triglycerides, fibrinogen, soluble IL-2 receptor, marrow) and treat its trigger
Involve infectious diseases early; isolate the patient while tuberculosis is possible
must_not_do: Diagnose sarcoidosis and start high-dose steroid without anti-tuberculosis cover while miliary tuberculosis has not been reliably excluded
Treat haemophagocytosis with etoposide or escalating immunosuppression alone without treating the trigger
Take a negative interferon-gamma release assay or negative smears as excluding miliary tuberculosis

rubric.5: Miliary (disseminated) tuberculosis with secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
rubric.4: Miliary tuberculosis without recognising the haemophagocytosis, or TB-associated HLH without naming the miliary form
rubric.3: Disseminated granulomatous infection (mycobacterial or fungal) not specified, with haemophagocytosis
rubric.2: Sarcoidosis, lymphoma or primary HLH as the final diagnosis
rubric.1: Unrelated diagnosis, or one that would lead to harm

gaps.item: Complete vital signs on admission (blood pressure, respiratory rate, SpO2)
gaps.guidance: Temperature and heart rate are reported. Blood pressure normal; respiratory rate mildly raised; SpO2 normal or mildly reduced on air at admission.

gaps.item: General and chest examination
gaps.guidance: Thin, unwell, febrile; mild pallor; lungs may be clear or have scattered fine crackles (miliary disease is often quiet on auscultation); no clubbing.

gaps.item: Abdominal examination and lymph nodes
gaps.guidance: Spleen palpable or not (moderate splenomegaly on CT); liver edge possibly palpable; no significant peripheral lymphadenopathy unless Atul decides otherwise.

gaps.item: Fundoscopy (choroidal tubercles)
gaps.guidance: Not reported. Do not invent a near-pathognomonic sign: the Case Reviewer decides; default no abnormality seen.

gaps.item: TB contact history, previous TB treatment, BCG vaccination, date of immigration
gaps.guidance: Not reported. No known contact and no previous treatment; BCG likely given in childhood; the Case Reviewer sets the immigration date.

gaps.item: Occupation, smoking, alcohol, drugs, sexual history, travel
gaps.guidance: Not reported. Neutral answers; no immunosuppressing risk (HIV negative).

gaps.item: Current medicines and allergies
gaps.guidance: None regular before admission; no known allergies.

gaps.item: Rest of the blood count on admission (MCV, lymphocytes, red cell indices) and day 17
gaps.guidance: The article says 'mild normocytic anaemia': MCV normal; lymphopenia likely. Day 17 consistent with Table 1 pancytopenia.

gaps.item: Inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR, procalcitonin)
gaps.guidance: The article says 'elevated inflammatory markers' without values: CRP and ESR raised; procalcitonin normal or mildly raised.

gaps.item: Renal function, electrolytes, bilirubin, ALP, albumin, LDH on admission
gaps.guidance: Renal function normal; sodium mildly low possible; albumin low; LDH raised; bilirubin and ALP normal or mildly raised on admission, rising by day 17.

gaps.item: Triglycerides and fibrinogen (H-score inputs)
gaps.guidance: Not reported although the H-score was 256: by day 17 triglycerides raised and fibrinogen low, consistent with that score; the Case Reviewer sets values.

gaps.item: Serum calcium, ACE, urine calcium (sarcoidosis work-up)
gaps.guidance: Not reported. Calcium normal; ACE normal or mildly raised (non-specific in granulomatous infection).

gaps.item: Blood cultures, including mycobacterial blood culture
gaps.guidance: Routine blood cultures negative. Mycobacterial blood culture: the Case Reviewer decides (the article does not report one).

gaps.item: Urine AFB and mycobacterial culture, and other extrapulmonary samples
gaps.guidance: Not reported. Do not auto-generate: the Case Reviewer sets them, since a positive result would end the case early.

gaps.item: AFB stain, PCR and mycobacterial culture on the bone marrow
gaps.guidance: Not reported. Do not auto-generate: the Case Reviewer decides; marrow culture is often positive in miliary disease but slow.

gaps.item: Liver biopsy
gaps.guidance: Not done in the article. If ordered: granulomas; the Case Reviewer decides AFB stain and culture results.

gaps.item: Lumbar puncture and CSF
gaps.guidance: Not done in the article. The Case Reviewer decides; default normal CSF or mild lymphocytosis.

gaps.item: Hepatitis B and C serology, EBV and CMV serology or PCR
gaps.guidance: Not reported individually ('viral work-up negative'): negative or past infection; EBV PCR negative.

gaps.item: Coagulation screen and arterial blood gas at day 18
gaps.guidance: Not reported. Coagulopathy with low fibrinogen; hypoxaemic respiratory failure with lactic acidosis in shock.

gaps.item: Bronchoscopy airway findings
gaps.guidance: Not reported. Airways normal or mildly inflamed; no endobronchial lesion.

gaps.item: Dates of the first-round tests, the steroid and the HLH treatment
gaps.guidance: The text gives no dates; Figure 5 (a timeline image) probably does. The Case Reviewer sets the days before path analysis.

gaps.item: Steroid drug and dose; etoposide dose
gaps.guidance: Not reported. High-dose steroid (for example prednisone 1 mg/kg or pulse methylprednisolone); HLH-2004 dexamethasone and etoposide doses.
